summary.rules:
(stated before scoring; see results/known_issue_recall.md for the per-issue table):
  * In scope: issues whose scope is `parser` or `template_or_history` (client/harness and out_of_scope issues are
    listed but not scored).
  * Executed projects: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, transformers. Only issues filed against these form the recall
    denominator ("strict recall"). Issues of projects we do not execute (Ollama — install blocked, LM Studio, MLX,
    LiteRT, model-hub template threads, ...) are reported as COVERED when a mapped case shows the reported failure
    mode on some executed path, else NOT COVERED; they never enter the denominator.
  * DETECTED: a mapped suite case (minimal repro X-*, fuzz subfamily, issue-derived case K-*) run on any executed
    version of the reported project gets a non-pass verdict from diff/analyze_x.judge() (defect or policy; the
    verdict is recorded), or, for template_or_history issues, the failure is reproduced by a template test
    (tests/test_template_equivalence.py, hand-verified mapping below) or by a history-study bug class whose
    failing component is the shared chat template or the reported project (history/results_history.json).
  * Evidence source is recorded: "blind" = cases that existed before the issue mapping (repros, fuzz families,
    template tests, history study); "issue-derived" = K-* cases written from the issue text or cases/runs added
    after the mapping (K-supp, the 0.24/0.27/0.29 family-E overlays, streaming scaling). Both recalls are reported.
  * Issues whose failing path or run mode the harness does not execute are listed in PATH_NOT_EXECUTED; they count
    as MISSES in the strict recall and are excluded only from the secondary path-matched recall.
  * The verdict rule above is MECHANICAL and credits any non-pass verdict on any mapped case, so a broadly mapped fuzz
    family can credit an unrelated failure. The HEADLINE is therefore the hand ADJUDICATED recall
    (known_issues/adjudication.json): an issue counts only when a suite case shows the failure the issue reports for
    the input form it describes; misses are classed as path/mode not executed, not reproduced on executed versions,
    or oracle gap; items reporting no concrete failure are excluded. The mechanical figure is reported as an upper
    bound only.
